audit.why: Level 3 gives you the root that answers his gap-close, level 6 gives Pop Blossom against Shadow Assault, his first lethality item is the one window where he one-combos you, and two items return the game to your AoE. spikes[0..3] carry this correctly.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blade's End is never mentioned anywhere on the page, and it is the single most punishable thing in his pattern: his spells stack Wound up to 3 times, and the heavy bleed only lands when he then BASIC ATTACKS a champion carrying 3 stacks. Also unstated: Noxian Diplomacy leaps only from outside melee range (575) and refunds health and cooldown when it kills, and Assassin's Path is free to cast but puts the vaulted terrain on a long cooldown for him.
audit.why: enemyKit P text: 'Talon's spells Wound champions... stacking up to 3 times. When Talon attacks a champion with 3 stacks of Wound, they bleed for heavy damage.' Q text: leap only from outside melee range, refunds health and cooldown on kill. E text: 'This ability has a low cooldown, but puts the used terrain on a long cooldown.'
audit.corrected: The bleed's auto-attack requirement, the 575 leap threshold, and the per-wall vault cooldown are now stated where they change a decision.

audit.why: Kit gives Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Noxian Diplomacy 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Assassin's Path 0 mana and 0 base cooldown with a per-terrain cooldown, Shadow Assault 100/80/60.

audit.why: ownerKit R is Pop Blossom; the near-miss detector matched on the apostrophe-s at distance 2.
audit.corrected: No edit. Recording it so a later pass does not 'fix' a correct name.

notes: CHART: content win[0..6] already matches packet.levelChart, so only the stale full-layer sides moved and no no-op win[N] edits were proposed. phases[5] is the only row that changed verdict direction and its why was rewritten in the same proposal; the other six moved toward Neeko, which their existing whys already argue. Ratings untouched — rows 0-3 read 'Talon' at 7/10 while 'Skill' rows read 6/10, so the scale is not legible enough to move safely. KIT FLAG CONTRADICTS RIOT TEXT: the brief flags 'knockup' on Rake (W), but Riot's description says the returning blades 'deal bonus damage and slow units hit' — no displacement. I asserted only the slow and the double pass; nothing on the page claimed a knockup, but flag it before someone adds one. FALSE POSITIVE CONFIRMED: packet.suspectNames flags "Pop Blossom's" in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name — it is correct, and no edit was made there. Blade's End was the biggest genuine gap: the three-stack bleed needs a basic attack to land, which is exactly what a root denies, and no field on the page mentioned the passive at all before this pass.
